chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad from Hariz, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who freed a slave who was shared between him and his partner.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'He has ruined the rights of his partner. If he has wealth, he gives half of the wealth [to the partner]; if he has no wealth, the slave is worked for: one day for the slave and one day for the master, and he employs him. And so it is if they are partners.'
And whenever the manumitter is causing harm and cannot afford the price of what remains of the slave, his manumission is invalid. He narrated that.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one partner frees a shared slave without the other's permission?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *kafāʾah* (compensation) in partial manumission, ensuring the partner's share is preserved either through liquid payment or proportional labor. The distinction between valid and invalid manumission based on the owner's financial capacity highlights the practical application of equity in shared property rights. This mechanism prevents unilateral actions from unfairly diminishing the partner's asset value, reflecting the broader Islamic legal emphasis on justice in commercial and familial transactions.
